followup_explanation:
I chose Dunlin-235B based on capability fit for this query, not the task-preference profiles.

This is a technical debugging task — interpreting an OpenCV traceback and explaining the fix. That's essentially a reasoning/extraction task: read the error, identify the cause (the assertion `!_src.empty()` means `cv2.imread` returned `None`, typically because the image path was wrong or the file didn't load), and explain the correction clearly.

Dunlin scores slightly higher on the benchmarks most relevant here:
- MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 79.6), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 61.8), Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 88.4) — general reasoning and technical problem-solving.
- Extraction & Retrieval (85.3 vs 83.6) — relevant for parsing the traceback.

Most of these gaps are within or near the stated variance threshold, so it's a close call, but Dunlin nudges ahead on the dimensions that matter for a precise, no-fluff technical answer (which is exactly what the user asked for: "без воды").

Petrel's strengths are in creative/generative work (Creative Generation 87.2), which isn't what this query needs. The task-preference notes for both models were irrelevant to the decision — they're self-reported preferences with no documented effect on output quality.
